label: early original-phase input from {t,m,o,p,i} right after a token from {m,p,t,i,1}
explanation: Fires mostly in the original phase (90% of mass), at steps 1-4 (peak at t=2), never at t=0. It is strongest when the current input is t, m, o, p or i AND the previous input (and to a lesser degree the one before) is m, p, t, i or 1; the top activations are prefixes like m m t, t m t, m t t. So it looks like a weighted count over an early-prefix token set. Activation grows when several of these tokens appear in a row, early in the sequence. Weak activity in the delimiter and copy phases (under 10% of mass). Rare on other letters, 0, and late original positions (t>=6). The conjunctive predicate reaches only about 0.5 F1 on dev, because the response is graded: single tokens from the set also fire weakly, and some pairs from the set do not fire.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: m, p, t, i, 1, 2; least: 3, b, f, e) and the current input token, by step (t=1: t, m, o, p; t=4: t, m, p, o; t=5: t, m, p, o); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, L=4 & t=3, L=3 & t=2.
